paper.title: RewardHarness: Self-Evolving Agentic Post-Training
paper.central_claim: A training-free, self-evolving agentic reward framework that reframes reward modeling as context evolution: from ~100 preference demonstrations it iteratively evolves a library of Skills and Tools (validation-gated) that, injected into a frozen VLM sub-agent, beats larger-data-trained reward models (EditReward) and GPT-5 on EditReward-Bench/GenAI-Bench and yields a better RL reward (FlowGRPO, ImgEdit-Bench 3.52).

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: no run receipt is exposed to the worker; model_type is the claude-kimi configured type.

materials.notes: Figures are caption-only in the text material (Fig. 6 curve values read from prose); no page images in manifest.

evidence.quote: training-free, self-evolving agentic reward framework that reframes reward modeling as context evolution rather than weight optimization
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: improvement object is a non-weight context (library), frozen sub-agent.

evidence.quote: The Library is initialized empty and grows through self-evolution
evidence.support_explanation: Pre-change state is an empty library; baseline for the retained change.

evidence.quote: by reading a Tool document, a general-purpose VLM can temporarily act as a specialized expert for a particular visual analysis task, without any parameter updates
evidence.support_explanation: Tools are Markdown procedural specs read by the VLM, not verified executable code.

evidence.quote: During inference, it examines the editing instruction and source image, then selects the appropriate Skills and Tools from the library
evidence.support_explanation: A Claude-based orchestrator is part of the inference-time system, not only the evolution loop.

evidence.quote: For errors, it performs root-cause analysis: identifying whether the failure stems from a missing evaluation criterion (suggesting a new Skill), an incorrect rubric application (suggesting a Skill modification), or a perceptual hallucination (suggesting a new or improved Tool).
evidence.support_explanation: Failure attribution from reasoning chains to create/modify edits.

evidence.quote: The proposal does not directly modify the committed Library.
evidence.support_explanation: Proposal is separated from commit via a candidate snapshot.

evidence.quote: An update is committed only when its validation accuracy strictly exceeds that of the current committed Library.
evidence.support_explanation: Commit rule: strict improvement on a ~30-example validation split, no paired test.

evidence.quote: only 8.1% of Skill proposals were accepted
evidence.support_explanation: Acceptance-rate (failed-candidate) information, but no absolute proposal counts.

evidence.quote: this final Library (3 Skills + 4 Tools) achieved 62.5% validation accuracy, a 47% relative improvement over the 42.5% empty-library baseline
evidence.support_explanation: Only library-on vs library-off contrast, but on the gating (selection) split.

evidence.quote: the pruning phase begins around iteration 50 after the library peaks at 13 entries (8 Skills + 5 Tools), eventually producing a compact final library with 7 entries (3 Skills + 4 Tools)
evidence.support_explanation: Library maintenance incl. deprecation/pruning.

evidence.quote: The 100 preference demonstrations are sampled exclusively from the training split of EditReward-Data, while EditReward-Bench is disjoint and used only for final evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Demo/test separation; no overlap audit against foundation-model pretraining.

evidence.quote: The three EditReward-Bench subsets contain 133, 450, and 888 pairwise comparisons, for 1,471 comparisons in total.
evidence.support_explanation: Denominators of the main benchmark; GenAI-Bench size not given.

evidence.quote: RewardHarness (Qwen) still outperforms EditReward (Qwen) by 3.7 points on average (45.7 vs. 42.0)
evidence.support_explanation: Main held-out comparison; single run, no CI; inference system differs (orchestrator + tools).

evidence.quote: The frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B model scores only 30.3 by itself, so the full system improves it by +15.4 points through the evolved Skills and Tools injected at test time.
evidence.support_explanation: Attribution of +15.4 to the library ignores the Claude orchestrator and secondary VLM calls.

evidence.quote: RewardHarness yields a larger overall improvement on ImgEdit-Bench, raising the base model from 3.32 to 3.52, whereas EditReward reaches 3.45
evidence.support_explanation: Downstream RL result; single FlowGRPO run each, no variance.
Base per-category scores (Add, Adjust, Extract, Replace, Remove, Bg, Style, Compose, Action, Overall).
Remove falls 2.90 to 2.19 and Action 4.44 to 4.22 after RL with RewardHarness reward, contradicting 'consistently improves'.

evidence.quote: improves editing quality while avoiding the reward hacking observed with supervised alternatives
evidence.support_explanation: Reward-hacking comparison is asserted; no reward-hacking analysis located in the text.

evidence.quote: a systematic characterization of the capability, API cost, latency, and deployment trade-offs across Orchestrator backbones remains future work
evidence.support_explanation: Cost/orchestrator dependence acknowledged and not measured.

evidence.quote: On the held-out MMMU validation set, accuracy improves from 79.6 to 80.7 (+1.1).
evidence.support_explanation: Only out-of-domain evidence; small, no variance, authors call it preliminary.

evidence.quote: co-evolve over 77 iterations of the self-evolution loop on the Gemini-2.0-Flash backbone
evidence.support_explanation: The shown evolution run used Gemini-2.0-Flash while the default Qwen result reuses the library; which backbone produced the committed library is not stated for Qwen.

evidence.quote: Validation accuracy plateaus at 52.5% as the library grows to 13 entries (8 Skills + 5 Tools), then improves after the pruning phase begins around iteration 50.
evidence.support_explanation: Evidence of bloat-plateau then pruning; best-of-iterations on a tiny validation set.

evidence.quote: it incurs substantial annotation cost, requires additional model training, often produces opaque scalar rewards, and is difficult to apply to closed or API-only foundation models
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap statement (annotation cost, training, opacity, API-only).

evidence.quote: Context-based self-evolving methods (Reflexion, ExpeL, Voyager, SkillRL, EvolveCoder) keep model weights fixed and evolve prompts, memories, or reusable skills
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest adjacent context-evolution family named, but no comparison to any of them or to prompt/rubric optimizers on the same 100 demos.

evidence.quote: Tools provide procedural grounding by routing specific sub-queries to a secondary VLM call.
evidence.support_explanation: Each tool use adds extra VLM calls at inference: extra, unreported cost.

signatures.object: Library of Skills (declarative Markdown rubrics) and Tools (procedural Markdown specs routed to a secondary VLM call) used as context for a frozen VLM reward judge; baseline = empty library.
signatures.information: Orchestrator sees sub-agent reasoning chains and ground-truth human preference rankings on ~70 train demos; ~30 demos are used only as validation gate; sub-agent (Qwen2.5-VL-7B / Gemini-2.0-Flash) sees images, instruction and selected library context; test benchmarks invisible.
signatures.operation: Evaluate on train split -> score vs human ranking -> chain analysis of correct and failed chains -> create/modify/deprecate proposal -> apply to candidate snapshot
signatures.conditions: Fixed iteration budget (about 77 iterations); N=100 demos.
signatures.feedback: Human preference labels on demos compared with sub-agent predicted rankings.
signatures.selection_rule: Commit only if validation accuracy strictly exceeds current committed library; otherwise discard and restore snapshot. Later aggressive pruning phase.
signatures.selection_data: Held-out validation split (~30 of the 100 demos) disjoint from the proposal/train split; same split reused each iteration.
signatures.persistence: Committed versioned library, frozen at end (iteration-69 library, 7 entries).
signatures.later_use: Orchestrator retrieves a subset of entries per new input; sub-agent reads them as context on held-out benchmarks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Avg pairwise accuracy 45.7 (Qwen) / 47.4 (Gemini) vs EditReward 42.0 / GPT-5 42.1; +15.4 over raw Qwen.
signatures.failure_boundary: Skill proposals accepted 8.1% vs Tool 41.4%; plateau at 52.5% with 13 entries before pruning; orchestrator dependence and cost unmeasured.

signatures.object: Frozen library-based reward model as RL reward for an image editor (FLUX.2-klein-base-4B via FlowGRPO); this updates editor weights, so it is a downstream utility check of the evaluator, not part of the retained non-weight loop.
signatures.information: Reward scores from RewardHarness vs EditReward; editor evaluated on ImgEdit-Bench.
signatures.conditions: Single run per reward; training prompts/data not described in the text.
signatures.persistence: not_applicable (weights of the editor change; library fixed).
signatures.failure_boundary: Remove and Action categories drop vs base; 'avoids reward hacking' not analysed.

gap.author_gap: Reward models for image editing need ~100K+ human preference labels, additional training, give opaque scalar rewards, and cannot be applied to API-only models, whereas humans learn the criteria from a few examples.
gap.checked_gap: The annotation-cost and API-only limits are real and sourced to prior reward-model work, but the 'fixed non-weight object' framing is thin: the changed object is the evaluator's context (library), and 'frozen model can improve via context' is background. The needed counterfactual (same 100 demos used in simpler ways) is absent.
gap.lineage: PickScore/ImageReward/VisionReward/EditReward (SFT reward models) -> context-evolution agents (Reflexion, ExpeL, Voyager, ACE, SkillRL) -> RewardHarness specialises context/skill evolution to multimodal reward judging; tool-augmented LLMs (ReAct, ToolLLM) assume fixed tool sets. Neighbours named from the paper only; no neighbour original text fixed in this batch.
gap.closest_adjacent: Rubric/skill/memory evolution for judges (ACE, ExpeL, SkillRL, Voyager); prompt optimisers (e.g. TextGrad/GEPA-style) are not discussed; few-shot in-context use of the same 100 demos not compared.
gap.residue: Whether library evolution (vs the Claude orchestrator, extra VLM tool calls, or simply few-shot prompting) delivers the gain; cost at inference; reward-hacking robustness.
gap.stakes: Annotation cost for 100K-scale preference data; usability with closed models.
gap.method_response: Failure-attributed library edits gated on a held-out validation split, producing an interpretable library that is frozen and reused.
gap.remaining_gap: Attribution to evolution, orchestrator dependence, cost, other domains (only a +1.1 MMMU hint).
unresolved: Closest adjacent methods not fixed or compared locally.
Which backbone produced the committed library used for the Qwen result (E021).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Conditioning substrate for the judge (rs) = evaluator artifact (Skills/Tools library) revised against a sparse human-label anchor (rsi H25): both put the task knowledge in editable context rather than weights.

pattern_mapping.differences: H25 evaluators are usually used for selection/audit; here the evaluator also serves as RL reward (H24-like use) with the library frozen; C03 assumes an upstream phase.

claims.text: Library evolved from 100 demos makes a frozen 7B VLM a better editing-reward judge than EditReward trained on 200K pairs.
claims.setting: EditReward-Bench K=2/3/4 + GenAI-Bench, Qwen2.5-VL-7B sub-agent, Claude orchestrator.
claims.baseline_control: EditReward (Qwen), GPT-5, raw Qwen; no orchestrator-only or few-shot control.
claims.selection_vs_test: Demos (train/val) from EditReward-Data train; test disjoint benchmark.
claims.result: 45.7 vs 42.0 avg; 133/450/888 pairwise comparisons for EditReward-Bench; single run.
claims.allowed_conclusion: The full orchestrated system outperforms the listed baselines on these benchmarks (author-reported); library-specific attribution is not isolated.

claims.text: The gated loop commits only improvements and converges to a compact 7-entry library.
claims.result: 62.5% val vs 42.5%; Skill acceptance 8.1%, Tool 41.4%; plateau 52.5% before pruning.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On the gating split the loop raised accuracy; the figure is optimistically selected.

claims.text: RewardHarness gives a better RL reward than EditReward and avoids reward hacking.
claims.baseline_control: Base and EditReward-reward runs under same pipeline.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small overall gain in one run; reward-hacking avoidance is not evidenced.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A Claude-orchestrated pipeline with a 7-entry Skills/Tools library gated on a ~30-example split and evolved from 100 EditReward demos reports 45.7/47.4 average accuracy on two disjoint reward benchmarks, above the listed baselines (author-reported, single run); one FlowGRPO run reports ImgEdit overall 3.52 vs 3.45 (EditReward).
assessment.not_supported: That library evolution (vs orchestrator/tool calls) causes the gain on held-out data; the 'avoids reward hacking' and cross-domain generality claims; cost-efficiency.
unresolved: Library-off test-set ablation under the same orchestrator
Backbone that produced the committed library

G.reason: Real limitation (annotation cost, opacity, API-only) but the closest context-evolution neighbours are only named, not compared, and the 'few demos suffice' premise lacks a same-demos baseline; residual bottleneck is only partly bounded.

M.reason: Loop is concrete: chain analysis maps error types to create/modify/deprecate edits, skills (declarative) vs tools (procedural, secondary-VLM calls) split is motivated by observed hallucination failures. Naive alternatives (few-shot with 100 demos, orchestrator alone) are not separated by a distinguishing prediction, so not 4.

X.reason: Operation chain, candidate-snapshot gate, restore and pruning are reconstructible; retrieval ('progressive disclosure') details, orchestrator model version, proposals per iteration and stopping rule are thin, no per-example regression check, and the backbone of the committed library is ambiguous.

E.measurement.reason: Established human-preference benchmarks with pairwise protocol and explicit comparison counts; no trivial/random baseline for K=3/4, GenAI-Bench size and ImgEdit judge not described in the text.

E.causality.reason: Only library-on/off contrast is on the gating split; the headline +15.4 vs raw Qwen conflates a Claude orchestrator and extra VLM tool calls; no gate-off, store-off on test, alternative optimiser or same-demos few-shot baseline; reward-hacking claim unsupported; RL gain small.

E.holdout.reason: Demos drawn from EditReward-Data train, test benchmarks disjoint and a second benchmark (GenAI-Bench); gating split separate from proposal split. No overlap audit with foundation-model pretraining; best-iteration selected on tiny reused validation split; scope beyond image editing only preliminary.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes and negative information (acceptance rates, plateau) are given but main results are single-run without CI/seeds; margins such as 45.7 vs 44.1 and 3.52 vs 3.45 are untested; validation set of ~40 comparisons.

E.cost.reason: Data budget (100 demos) and iteration count (77) reported; orchestrator/API cost, inference overhead (orchestrator + secondary VLM calls) and matched-budget baselines are explicitly left to future work.
